title: When was the bite?
hook: A mark on bone can leave more than one history.

knows: Some animals bite and scavengers can feed on remains.
doesNotKnow: Separate a bone-contact observation from an unsupported timing claim.

misconception: A bite mark on bone always proves that the animal was hunted while alive.
objective: Separate a bone-contact observation from an unsupported timing claim.

claims.text: A mark on bone can leave more than one history. A fossil bone has confirmed bite marks. Without other evidence, what can you infer about the bite relative to the animal’s death? The same kind of bite mark could be made before death or by feeding on remains after death. A confirmed mark records contact with bone; its timing needs additional evidence. A mark alone does not prove a hunt.
claims.source: Source lead for independent checking: Smithsonian https://naturalhistory.si.edu/collections/paleobiology. The two histories are logical possibilities, not reconstructions of a real fossil.
